docs.title: 7627 Software Docs
docs.text: Welcome to the 7627 software documentation hub! Use the navigation sidebar or top tabs to click through the documentation. If you are new to the 7627 software team, visit Onboarding.

docs.title: What does software do?
docs.text:
A robot that has merely been designed, built, and wired is not capable of anything. The missing piece is software, and it is your job as part of the software team to produce that missing piece. This will consist of two primary responsibilities:

  • Firmware Management - As a prerequisite to ensure the software can talk to the hardware, the firmware must be properly installed and configured.

  • Programming - To give the robot the instructions it needs in a form the it can understand, the robot must be programmed. We use the Java programming language for robot code. If you don't know how to program, in Java or at all, worry not! This documentation contains all the resources you will need to know.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
You will need a laptop(not a Chromebook! Ideally a Windows laptop, although Linux may work) and access to unrestricted Internet(not school managed Wi-Fi! Use a mobile hotspot or VPN). Then, make sure you already have, or otherwise install, the following applications:

  • WPILib - An indispensable library and development environment for FRC software.

  • NI Tools - This will include all the basic apps you need to run a robot including Driver Station and the roboRIO imaging tool. Note, you will need to create an NI account, but luckily it is free.

  • RoboRIO Imaging Tool - Packaged within NI tools, but is essential for roboRIO operation(Systemcore will replace roboRIO as of the 2027 season). It primarily allows you to update or start anew on a roboRIO.

  • A flashing software of your choice. Some options are listed below:

  • Balena Etcher - Works, although deprecated.

  • Raspberry Pi Imager - Possibly works.

  • Rev Hardware Client - This is used to interface with REV hardware such as SparkMAXs.

  • Rev Hardware Client 2 - If your REV hardware is too new or you need some specific feature use this.

  • Phoenix Tuner X - Used to interface with CTRe hardware such as Krakens.

  • PathPlanner - A GUI program for easily creating paths for autonomous operation.

  • AdvantageScope - Primarily useful for playing back past logs, indispensable for troubleshooting.

docs.title: New to programming in Java?
docs.text:
You will also need to know how to program in Java. Some useful tutorials are listed below:

  • W3 Schools Java Tutorial - Teaches the fundamentals of Java. You don't need any programming knowledge to follow the tutorial.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
Each of the following are good next places to learn more about software. You can visit each in any order:

  • Installing and Configuring Firmware - A guide for dealing with firmware setup.

  • Programming for 7627 - A guide more focused on the particulars of programming for the team.

  • Troubleshooting - A guide for when things go wrong.

  • Who you gonna call? - A guide for determining who you need to ask for information.

  • Glossary - A guide for the various jargon you will eventually need to know.

  • Technical Documentation - Detailed documentation about our codebase, a good reference for if you need information concerning the codebase itself.
